deep.reconstruction:
OVERVIEW. This page is an exploratory calculation in the heat-conduction bundle. It works with two variables r, s and a function a = a(r,s) (also written α). Two auxiliary coefficients b, c appear, along with a function γ. The following page studies u_t = a u_ββ + b u_β + c u_αβ + e u_α and separation/transformation of such equations. That fits the reading that Riemann is asking when a second-order operator in (r,s) admits a companion operator, i.e. a commutation, factorization or compatibility condition. He then reduces the resulting condition on the zeroth-order coefficient c to characteristic coordinates.

(1) Top line. An isolated fifth-order nonlinear expression:
α_{srrrr} + α_{ssrr} + α_{sss} − 2 α_{sr} α_{rrr} − 4 α_{rr} α_{srr}.
It is probably a compatibility expression obtained by eliminating γ. It has no '= 0' and is not used further.

(2) The linear equation γ_rr + γ_s + α_rr γ = 0. This is a backward heat / imaginary-time Schrödinger equation with potential α_rr.

(3) Two operators are written down.
- First operator, roughly L = ∂_r² ± ∂_s² + 2a_r ∂_r + b.
- Second operator, roughly M = ∂_s + a_s ∂_r + c. The exact form is partly illegible.
- The side condition b_r = 2c_s is recorded.

Riemann then lists the coefficients of the commutator- or compatibility-type expression, order by order:
- ∂_r²: 2a_rs − 2a_rs = 0.
- ∂_r∂_s: 2(a_rr − a_ss).
- ∂_r: 2a_rss + b_s − a_rrs − a_sss + 2a_s a_ss − 2a_r a_sr − 2c_r.
- ∂_s: b_r − 2c_s (plus an illegible term).
- Zeroth order: b_rs + a_s b_r − c_rr − c_ss − 2a_r c_r.

Using b_r = 2c_s (my filling: b_rs = 2c_ss, a_s b_r = 2a_s c_s), the zeroth-order condition becomes
c_ss − c_rr + 2a_s c_s − 2a_r c_r + 2c(a_ss − a_rr) = 0. (*)

(4) Potentials. He sets c = γ_sr and b = 2γ_ss. This satisfies b_r = 2c_s identically. Substituting into the ∂_r-coefficient gives
−a_rrs − a_sss + 2a_ss a_s − 2a_r a_sr = 2∂_s(γ_rr − γ_ss).

(5) Characteristic coordinates. With s = p+q and r = p−q he notes ∂_p = ∂_s + ∂_r and ∂_p∂_q = ∂_s² − ∂_r². Then (*) becomes the Laplace-type hyperbolic equation
c_pq + c_p a_q + c_q a_p + 2c a_pq = 0.
It can be written in conservation form as c_pq + (a_q c)_p + (a_p c)_q = 0.

(6) Eliminating c_p. He puts c_pq = −β, so β = a_q c_p + a_p c_q + 2a_pq c. My reconstruction of the step: divide by a_q, differentiate in q, use c_pq = −β, and multiply by a_q². This gives
β_q a_q + β(a_q² − a_qq) = c_qq a_p a_q + c_q(3a_pq a_q − a_qq a_p) + c(2a_pqq a_q − 2a_pq a_qq).
Riemann writes the last two terms under c_q and c respectively. This is an equation in c, c_q, c_qq only.

An earlier attempt at this step is struck out.

(7) He begins to differentiate this relation in p and multiply by a_q, to eliminate further and get an equation for β (or a) alone. The last two lines break off unfinished.
errors: In the step from the ∂_r-coefficient to the γ-equation (step 4), the term 2∂³a/∂r∂s² listed first in the ∂_r line does not reappear. Either it was cancelled or misread (it may be 2∂³a/∂r²∂s, which would change the sign of the a_rrs term), or Riemann dropped it. The page as read is not fully consistent here.
Step 6 checks out exactly: β_q a_q + β(a_q² − a_qq) − RHS = a_q²(c_pq + β), which vanishes by the definition of β.
The final lines (differentiating with respect to p) are incomplete and partly garbled. The written RHS '= c_qq a_pp (a_q)² + ...' breaks off and cannot be verified.
The exact operators L, M are not fully legible. The ∂_r∂_s coefficient 2(a_rr − a_ss) shows the second-order parts were not the plain Laplacian with ∂_r∂_s, so the precise setup remains uncertain.

results.what: Transformation of the condition on c to characteristic coordinates s=p+q, r=p−q, giving c_pq + a_q c_p + a_p c_q + 2a_pq c = 0
results.modern_name: Reduction of a linear hyperbolic PDE to characteristic (null) coordinates; Laplace-type equation in conservation form
results.usually_credited_to: Euler/Laplace (18th c.); standard; Riemann 1860 used characteristic form for hyperbolic equations

results.what: Elimination of c_p by dividing by a_q and differentiating in q, giving an equation in c, c_q, c_qq and β
results.modern_name: Elimination step akin to the Laplace cascade / Laplace invariants method

results.what: Commutation/compatibility conditions of two variable-coefficient differential operators, order by order, related to a heat/Schrödinger-type equation γ_rr + γ_s + α_rr γ = 0
results.modern_name: Operator commutation or compatibility conditions (cf. later Lax-pair-style computations), here exploratory
results.usually_credited_to: General method; systematic theory of commuting differential operators: Burchnall–Chaundy (1920s)

deep.surprise_reason: These are mainly routine variable changes and elimination computations on unpublished scratch work related to transforming heat-conduction equations. The commutator-type computation tied to a Schrödinger/heat operator with potential α_rr, and the nonlinear fifth-order expression, are mildly intriguing. However, they are unfinished and their exact setup is unclear, so nothing here clearly anticipates a later named result.

transcription_corrections: In the eliminated-equation line the bracket is β((∂a/∂q)² − ∂²a/∂q²). In the final long line the transcription drops the inner parentheses, writing β(∂a/∂q)² − ∂²a/∂q².
The second row under the long equation consists of coefficients aligned under the c_q and c terms: −a_qq a_p multiplies ∂c/∂q, and −2a_pq a_qq multiplies c.
In the last long line, '∂a/∂p∂q' should be ∂²a/∂p∂q.
The top-right marginal notes read ∂c/∂p = ∂c/∂s + ∂c/∂r and ∂²c/∂p∂q = ∂²c/∂s² − ∂²c/∂r², with s = p+q and r = p−q. These are correct.

The leading sign/coefficient of the final (*) line (the transcription has '+4'/'+2'?) is likely just '+'. The result c_ss − c_rr + 2a_s c_s − 2a_r c_r + 2c(a_ss − a_rr) = 0 matches the p,q form exactly.
The operator lines '∂_r²+∂_s²+2a_r∂_r+b = ∂_s+' and '∂_s + a_s∂_r + c' are partly illegible. The first may involve ∂_r² − ∂_s² or a product of operators.
